technical_and_design_decisions: The increment is implemented on top of the existing Spring XD distributed runtime codebase (admin nodes, container nodes, OOTB modules/jobs, servers.yml configuration), extended to run as Docker containers.

U1: External service linking (RabbitMQ, Redis, Zookeeper, Hadoop, MongoDB) is implemented via Docker environment variables and container link attributes; container entrypoint scripts map these environment variables onto Spring XD configuration (servers.yml / module properties) at startup.

U2: Service discovery is built on Zookeeper, which Spring XD already uses for runtime coordination; containers register their host/port endpoints and admin nodes discover container and external service locations dynamically, with guidance for Consul/etcd-style alternatives documented.

U3: Docker images for XD admin and container nodes are built by the CI server from versioned Dockerfiles; the CI pipeline builds the distribution, assembles images, runs automated image smoke tests (container startup, node registration, simple stream/job deployment), tags, and pushes images to the Docker registry per environment.

U4: Mesos deployment uses Marathon application group definitions (JSON) with placement constraints and health checks for XD admin and container nodes; the deliverable is documentation plus validated sample Marathon descriptors, with the recommendations verified on a test Mesos/Marathon cluster.

U5: The Spring Boot dependency upgrade is performed in the build, compilation/deprecation issues are resolved, and the existing automated test suite plus targeted regression tests are run to confirm no functional side effects; findings are documented.

U6: The data partitioning strategy for RDBMS-to-HDFS ingest is exposed as job module options (e.g., partition column, number of partitions, ranges) built on the existing partitioned-job support (Spring Batch partitioning) so ingest steps execute in parallel.

U7: The HDFS source module is implemented as a new Spring XD stream source module that reads files from HDFS using the existing Hadoop/HDFS client integration, with options for name-node URI, directory, and file-name pattern, and it emits file contents as stream messages.

U8: A new commit-interval property is added to servers.yml with the current default preserved; the value is propagated to all out-of-the-box jobs that support partitioning, with the ability to override per job deployment.

All code is written in Java following the existing Spring XD conventions; unit tests are included within development activities, while integration/system verification is covered by dedicated test activities.
assumptions: A single developer performs all work; estimates are in ideal workdays of 8 hours and exclude elapsed-time effects such as waiting on environments or reviews.
The existing Spring XD codebase, its Gradle build, and a CI server with Docker build capability are already available and operational.

Test infrastructure is available at no setup cost within the estimates: Docker Engine and registry, a Mesos/Marathon test cluster, a Hadoop/HDFS cluster, and instances of RabbitMQ, Redis, Zookeeper, and MongoDB.

The Spring Framework/Spring Boot versions used are the ones aligned with the Spring XD dependency baseline targeted by this increment; the Spring 6/Java 17 background information does not mandate a Java 17 migration for this increment.
U4 is documentation-only in scope but includes hands-on validation of the recommended deployment on the Mesos/Marathon test cluster.
U5 covers evaluation of the upgrade plus the remediation needed to keep existing functionality working, not a redesign of features for the new Boot version.
No user-interface work is required; all configuration is file/CLI/environment-variable based.
Documentation deliverables (U1 pointers, U4 guide) are written by the developer as part of this increment.
Unit testing effort is embedded in development activities; integration and end-to-end testing are separate listed activities.
The eight user stories constitute the complete scope of the software increment.

activities.activity_name: Requirements analysis and overall solution design
activities.activity_description: Analyze the eight user stories, confirm scope, and produce the overall design: Docker configuration approach, service discovery approach, CI image pipeline design, partitioning option design, HDFS source module design, and servers.yml property changes.

Set up local build of the Spring XD codebase, Docker tooling, local Zookeeper/RabbitMQ/Redis/Mongo/HDFS endpoints, and access to the CI server and test clusters needed for development and verification.

activities.activity_name: U1: Implement Docker container configuration for external service linking
activities.activity_description: Implement entrypoint scripts and configuration templates so XD containers can be linked/bound to external services (RabbitMQ, Redis, Zookeeper, Hadoop, MongoDB) via Docker link attributes and environment variables mapped onto XD configuration; unit test the mapping logic.

activities.activity_name: U1: Document linking attributes and environment variables
activities.activity_description: Write the user-facing documentation with pointers to the supported linking/binding attributes and the environment variables recognized by the XD container images, including examples per external service.
Design how XD processes and services in a Docker cluster register and discover one another using Zookeeper-backed service registration/discovery, including configuration knobs and failure behavior.

Implement the service discovery integration for XD containers: registration of container/admin endpoints, discovery of external service locations, and the related configuration properties; add unit tests.

activities.activity_name: U2: Test service discovery in cluster scenarios
activities.activity_description: Verify discovery behavior across multi-container scenarios: nodes joining/leaving, service relocation, restart recovery, and correct routing of traffic between discovered services.

activities.activity_name: U3: Create Dockerfiles for XD images
activities.activity_description: Author versioned Dockerfiles for XD admin and container images that package all required components and default configurations, integrating the U1 environment-variable configuration support.

activities.activity_name: U3: Set up CI pipeline for image build, test, and publish
activities.activity_description: Configure the CI build to compile the distribution, build Docker images from the Dockerfiles, run automated image smoke tests, tag images, and push them to the registry for the various target environments.

activities.activity_name: U3: Validate image testing and deployment to environments
activities.activity_description: Exercise the pipeline end to end: deploy CI-built images to representative environments, run stream/job smoke deployments, and fix pipeline or image defects found.

activities.activity_name: U4: Validate and document Mesos/Marathon XD cluster deployment
activities.activity_description: Deploy an XD cluster on the Mesos test cluster using Marathon application definitions, validate behavior (placement, scaling, health checks), and write the recommendations document including sample Marathon descriptors.

activities.activity_name: U5: Evaluate Spring Boot dependency upgrade
activities.activity_description: Upgrade the Spring Boot dependency in the build, resolve compilation/deprecation/behavior conflicts, run the existing automated test suite plus targeted regression checks to confirm no side effects, and document the impact assessment.

activities.activity_name: U6: Implement data partitioning strategy option for RDBMS-to-HDFS ingest
activities.activity_description: Add job module options allowing users to supply a partitioning strategy (partition column, partition count, ranges) that parallelizes the RDBMS-to-HDFS ingest using the existing partitioned-job infrastructure; include unit tests.

Integration-test the partitioning option with representative databases and data volumes: verify correct split of work, parallel execution, completeness of ingested data in HDFS, and behavior with invalid strategies.

Develop the new HDFS source stream module that ingests data directly from HDFS (name-node URI, directory, file pattern options) and emits contents into the stream, including module metadata and unit tests.
Integration-test the HDFS source against the Hadoop test cluster: file discovery, large-file handling, error paths (missing directory, connectivity loss), and end-to-end stream delivery.

activities.activity_name: U8: Implement and test commit-interval override
activities.activity_description: Add the commit-interval property to servers.yml with the existing default preserved, propagate it to all out-of-the-box jobs with partition support, allow per-job override, and test across the affected OOTB jobs.

Run full end-to-end verification of the increment: Dockerized XD cluster with external services and service discovery, CI-built images, partitioned RDBMS-to-HDFS ingest, HDFS source streams, and commit-interval behavior, fixing defects found.

activities.activity_name: Final documentation review and release packaging
activities.activity_description: Consolidate all documentation (U1 pointers, U4 Mesos/Marathon guide, U5 upgrade impact notes, new module/job option references), finalize release notes, and package the increment for release.
